epics.title: Protocol Access Control for Researchers
epics.jtbd: When a user accesses protocols, I want access to be restricted to Researchers and above, so that the archive role model is enforced as specified.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: Zero unauthorized access incidents to protocols
requirements: R1: Restrict protocol access to users with RESEARCHER, EPIDEMIOLOGIST, or ADMIN roles.

slices.title: Implement Protocol Access Control
slices.jtbd: When implementing protocol access control for this epic, I want to restrict access to authorized roles, so that unauthorized users cannot view protocols.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given an authenticated user,
When they attempt to access protocols,
Then access is granted only if their role is RESEARCHER, EPIDEMIOLOGIST, or ADMIN.
Given automated tests, When verifying protocol access, Then both authorized and unauthorized access paths are covered.
slices.sixSigmaMetric: 100% enforcement of role-based access to protocols

epics.title: Strains Catalog Pagination
epics.jtbd: When fetching the catalog of strains, I want the results to be paginated, so that the endpoint does not suffer from performance degradation as data grows.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: Endpoint response time under 200ms for large catalogs
requirements: R1: Implement pagination on the /api/v1/strains endpoint accepting page and size parameters.

slices.title: Add Pagination to Strains Catalog Endpoint
slices.jtbd: When implementing pagination for this epic, I want to accept page and size parameters, so that the catalog endpoint can scale.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a request to /api/v1/strains,
When returning the list of accessible strains,
Then the response is paginated (accepting page and size parameters).
Given an automated test suite, When evaluating the strains endpoint, Then proper pagination behavior is verified.
slices.sixSigmaMetric: Consistent sub-200ms response time for paginated strains query

requirements: R1: Split comma-separated user courses and use a strict IN clause instead of LIKE %course% for authorization.

slices.title: Fix Insecure Authorization via Fuzzy Substring Matching
slices.jtbd: When implementing strict course matching for this epic, I want to use a strict IN clause instead of fuzzy matching, so that access control is exact and secure.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a comma-separated list of user courses,
When executing the authorization JPQL query,
Then the courses are split into a Java List and matched using a strict IN clause instead of LIKE %course%.
Given automated tests for the JPQL query, When testing access control, Then strict exact matching is verified against fuzzy false-positives.
slices.sixSigmaMetric: Zero authorization false positives due to fuzzy matching
